newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs fall on SIMEX due to Sakakibara remarks.
newsitem.headline: JGBs fall on SIMEX due to Sakakibara remarks.

text.p: The key June 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract fell on the Singapore International Monetary Exchange after the close of Tokyo's morning session on Friday.
Traders said the fall was due to comments by Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of the ministry's International Finance Bureau.
Sakakibara told Reuters Financial Television that the JGB market is too bubbly and contains risk of bursting.
The June stood at 126.50 on SIMEX as of 0254 GMT. The June ended Tokyo's morning session at 126.79.
Sakakibara also said the possibility that the Japanese economy will contract is less than people think, and added that it is dangerous to assume Japan will not raise interest rates within a year.
Traders in Tokyo said the impact on JGBs is likely to be limited, as Sakakibara's comments did not seem very new.

"He said similar things on Wednesday, and taking into account that JGBs have been solidly supported on the downside recently, I don't think a huge fall is likely. But sentiment may worsen if the June breaks below 126.50 and then 126.41 in Tokyo," a trader for a city bank's securities unit said.
Sakakibara said on Wednesday in a speech to currency dealers he could not comprehend why Japan's long-term interest rates were at their current record-low levels.
Sakakibara said that although monetary policy was in the hands of the Bank of Japan, there was political pressure to raise the official discount rate.
"Some politicians have called for a rise in the official discount rate. It is true that there is an atmosphere among politicians to raise the official discount rate," he said.
